subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should elevated cron/heartbeat authority be implemented as narrow per-job and heartbeat markers now, or folded into the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance design?
rationale: The source gap is real, but choosing where trusted authority is created, stored, audited, migrated, and enforced changes the elevated host-exec trust boundary and upgrade behavior for existing cron and heartbeat users.

options.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
options.body: Treat elevated execution as part of the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance design so cron APIs, heartbeat state, audit, and upgrade handling share one authority model.

options.title: Implement Narrow Markers
options.body: Add per-job and heartbeat-specific elevated approval metadata now, with execution-time checks and docs, while leaving broader scheduling provenance to a later RFC.

options.title: Fail Closed For Internal Sources
options.body: Remove wildcard internal-source elevation by default and require explicit operator opt-in, accepting upgrade friction for existing cron and heartbeat setups.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
recommendation.body: Treat elevated execution as part of the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance design so cron APIs, heartbeat state, audit, and upgrade handling share one authority model.

likelyOwner.reason: They recently owned the adjacent Gateway and agent cron caller-scope implementation that this trust-boundary change would need to extend.
